headline: Stochastic models validated against gait, neuronal, and calcium dynamics data
label: Stochastic Dynamics Model Validation
summary: Model comparison on gait, neuron, and calcium data tests whether stochastic models capture long memory, transitions, and state structure.
synthesis: The common thread is testing stochastic models against time-series data through formal discrimination between candidate descriptions. In the gait study, ARFIMA model comparison on stride series from 70 subjects indicates cued anti-persistence is genuine long memory, and DFA overestimates d by 0.5. A 5D CA1 neuron with bounded M-current noise shows coherence resonance and noise-activated firing transitions. A deep learning classifier (LKCNN) trained on Langevin-simulated data distinguishes eight stochastic intracellular Ca2+ dynamical states at 96.8% accuracy. The items differ in data source and method, so the dominant thread is explicit stochastic formulation as a testable hypothesis, with the calcium study the only one reporting classification performance.
